messages:
Amy: Heads-up — enterprise prospect (FinRegCo) just asked for feature parity on our auth-by-policy routing before we can close. They want a firm ship date for parity vs 'premium routing' features. Can product lead weigh in?
Sam: Are they asking for exact policy grammar parity (ACLs, role mapping), or just the UI/SDK surface?
Amy: They called out two asks: 1) same per-tenant routing rules as competitor (policy DSL + fallbacks) and 2) audit-log parity (per-request routing decision metadata).
Jordan: Important: parity here = blocking for the deal. If we push premium features later we need clear rollback/fallback and docs for sales.
Lee: Quick feasibility: runtime already supports routing hooks and fallbacks, but policy DSL support + config UI will take ~2 sprints for eng + 1 sprint for console. Audit metadata is smaller, could be toggled behind flag.
Nina: From sales: FinRegCo is a $350k ARR ARR expansion potential, timeline is EOY. They want a commitment. Sales needs a PRD + launch criteria to show to legal and procurement.
Sam: Proposal: ship minimal parity (policy DSL subset + audit metadata + docs + sales playbook) as an "Enterprise Parity 1.0". Defer UX polish and advanced premium rules to later. Launch criteria:
- runtime correctness on policy subset (unit + e2e)
- audit logs include decision_id, matched_rule, fallback_reason
- perf SLO: < 5ms additional routing latency p50 on 90% of requests
- docs+sales playbook published
- gated behind feature flag and enterprise tier only
Jordan: +1. Add rollback plan: automatic fallback to simple routing policy and incident runbook.
Lee: Engineering estimate: parity-1.0 API + runtime + flag = 6 dev-weeks (2 engs full time) + 1 week QA. Console subset + docs = 3 dev-weeks (1 eng) parallel.
Amy: Risk check: this increases token path checks slightly. Need to validate cost delta on typical workload. Assign to eng-infra for perf profiling.
Sam: I'll draft a short PRD template. Key sections: customer ask, acceptance criteria (matching your launch criteria), rollout plan, sales enablement checklist, metrics to monitor. Will post by EOD.
Nina: Sales enablement checklist (minimum): one-pager for procurement, demo checklist, competitive talking points (mapping vs competitor), legal checklist for audit log retention.
Jordan: Metrics to monitor for first 30 days: routing latency P50/P95, feature flag usage by tenant, errors caused by policy parse, cost delta per 1M tokens. Thresholds: if P95 > 200ms or cost delta > 8% -> pause rollout.
Lee: Sample rollout policy we can use (config):
```
rollout:
  feature: enterprise_parity_1
  percent: 10
  criteria:
    latency_p95: 200ms
    error_rate: 0.1%
```
Amy: Who owns the PRD and timeline commitment? I'm happy to own product PRD + legal check. Jordan and Lee to own runtime acceptance tests and rollout automation. Sam to own sales playbook.
Sam: I'll coordinate with Nina to prep procurement one-pager and handoff to AE.
Jordan: Can eng-infra do a quick perf profile this week? If perf looks good we can confirm 2-sprint plan.
Lee: Eng-infra pinged deploy-bot for a perf job, they scheduled a bench run for tomorrow. deploy-bot: scheduled run started at 1768001250.
deploy-bot: perf-run finished at 1768001275 — baseline delta 3.8% median cost, p95 latency +4ms, failure rate unchanged. Detailed logs: https://internal/run/1768001275
Nina: Good initial signal. Sales: we'll tell FinRegCo we can commit to a scoped parity-1.0 by +8 weeks with the gated rollout and SLA language. Need final sign-off from Eng/Prod.
Amy: Decision: move forward with Parity-1.0 scoped plan. Action items: Sam PRD by EOD, Lee/Jordan finalize tests and rollout automation, Nina to update AE and procurement. We'll reconvene next Wed to check progress. :thumbsup:
Sam: PRD link posted: https://docs.redwood/prd/enterprise-parity-1768001234 (draft). Feedback welcome.
Lee: I'll open the engineering epic and attach estimates.
Jordan: Adding monitoring alerts now.
Amy: Thanks everyone. Closing thread for now. We can reopen if any blockers pop up. :eyes:
